cards.lore: Dino drives the Reward Road. Block him to stop the voices, but watch out for the Parkinsonian Rust.
cards.power: The Euphoria Spike. Too much in the mesolimbic track = Hallucinations. Too little in the mesocortical track = Flat affect.

cards.lore: When Sally leaves the ring, the world turns grey. SSRIs act as vacuum plugs to keep her in the synaptic gap longer.
cards.power: The Rhythm Keeper. Controls sleep, appetite, and the will to wrestle.

cards.lore: Benzodiazepines strengthen Garry's grip. A sudden withdrawal means brain on fire (seizures).
cards.power: The Big Chill. Tells the neurons to shut up and relax.

cards.lore: Too much Gus leads to excitotoxicity. Ketamine blocks Gus to perform a hard system reset.
cards.power: The Spark. Gus is Garry's archnémesis. He turns on the lights and lets the sparks fly.

cards.lore: Driven by Dino's rampage in the mesolimbic system. Requires at least 1 core symptom: delusion, hallucination, or disorganized speech.
cards.power: The Delusion Bubble. Sam creates a reality where only he knows the rules.

cards.lore: Sid is a border-crosser. He must prove his psychosis can exist even without the emotional roller coaster.
cards.power: The Dual Threat. A dangerous mix of Sam's delusions and Barry's mood swings.

cards.lore: A temporary system failure. Berty returns completely to his old self after the match concludes.
cards.power: The Snap. A sudden break with reality, usually after a traumatic match.

cards.lore: Aside from his one quirk, Dan functions perfectly. He's not schizophrenic; he's just extremely stubborn.
cards.power: The Unshakable Belief. Dan firmly believes the referee loves him or the FBI is hunting him.

cards.lore: During mania, Barry needs no sleep and spends all his gold tokens. He thinks he is the invincible champion.
cards.power: The Flight of Ideas. Builds a skyscraper ego in one night or feels like a crushed bug.

cards.lore: Massive withdrawal of Sally and Nora. The world loses its color and value.
cards.power: The Gravity Well. Debbie makes every movement an ordeal. Even breathing feels like wrestling against lead.

cards.lore: A chronic state of not-quite-happiness. She is the rain that never stops.
cards.power: The Eternal Grey. Polly isn't as heavy as Debbie, but she never goes away.

cards.lore: The lite version of Barry. Most unstable character on the roster, but always stays in the ring.
cards.power: The Constant Ripple. Cy is never stable, but his waves are small enough to stay out of the hospital.

cards.lore: A false alarm from Norepi-Nora. Pete thinks he's dying even though he's just standing in a supermarket.
cards.power: The Suffocator. Pete makes the heart race and the throat tighten with no opponent in the ring.

cards.lore: Often the result of Pete's attacks. Abby shrinks her world until only her house remains.
cards.power: The Locker Room Lockdown. Abby fears places where she cannot escape quickly.

cards.lore: The action (compulsion) only serves to temporarily silence the agonizing thought (obsession).
cards.power: The Endless Reset. Otto must tie his shoes 50 times, otherwise the stadium will explode.

cards.lore: The brain has not archived the trauma. It remains an open wound that can tear again at any time.
cards.power: The Time Warp. Paul is catapulted back into his worst match by a sound or a smell.

cards.lore: Effective but brutal. Causes EPS (extrapyramidal symptoms) — the wrestler becomes stiff as a statue.
cards.power: The Dopamine Handcuffs. Hali chains up the Dino and stops delusions immediately.

cards.lore: She is the queen, but dangerous. Can eat white blood cells. For expert matches under supervision only!
cards.power: The Ultimate Override. The only one who wins when all other antipsychotics have failed.

cards.lore: Blocks dopamine and serotonin simultaneously. Modern approach with less rust than Hali.
cards.power: The Prolactin Leak. Dampens psychosis but lets hormones go wild (gynecomastia/lactation).

cards.lore: Blocks histamine receptors, leading to insatiable hunger and insulin resistance.
cards.power: The Metabolic Expansion. Stops voices but makes the wrestler twice as heavy within weeks.

cards.lore: Needs 4-6 weeks to warm up. Side effect: the Sexual Snag (loss of libido).
cards.power: The Vacuum Plug. Plugs the drains so Sally can stay in the ring longer.

cards.lore: At high doses, Venny pushes blood pressure up. Good for Debbie when she has no energy left.
cards.power: The Double Boost. Brings both Sally AND Nora back into the fight.

cards.lore: The Old Guard. Unpopular due to anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation).
cards.power: The Dirty Bomb. Hits everything: serotonin, norepi, histamine, acetylcholine. Extremely effective but toxic in overdose.

cards.lore: Tyramine danger! If Mao blocks tyramine breakdown, blood pressure explodes (hypertensive crisis).
cards.power: The Forbidden Feast. Prevents breakdown of all transmitters. Warning: no cheese, no wine!

cards.lore: Lou hates the thyroid and kidneys. Narrow therapeutic window — too much Lou is pure poison.
cards.power: The Suicidal Shield. The only one who can truly anchor Barry's seesaw to the ground.

cards.lore: Absolute ban for pregnant wrestlers! Causes hair loss and weight gain.
cards.power: The Mania Muzzler. Helps Garry calm the ring down. Especially good for mixed states.

cards.lore: High addiction potential! Like a loan — solves the problem now, but you pay with interest (withdrawal).
cards.power: The Instant Off-Switch. When Pete panics or Barry riots, Lora sends them to sleep immediately.

cards.lore: Because of the long action, Diaz accumulates in the body. He is the marathon runner of benzos.
cards.power: The Smooth Landing. Used to bring wrestlers safely through alcohol withdrawal.

cards.lore: Not psychotic; just extremely suspicious. Reads hostile intent into harmless comments.
cards.power: The Conspiracy Theory. Thinks everyone in the crowd and his partner wants to betray him.

cards.lore: Isn't shy — he just doesn't care. Considers neither praise nor criticism important.
cards.power: The Void of Interest. Wants no friends, no dates, no fans. Prefers wrestling in an empty stadium.

cards.lore: Sam's eccentric cousin. No hallucinations, but his reality is very... specific.
cards.power: The Strange Vibe. Wears odd clothes and claims he can read the thoughts of the ring posts.

cards.lore: The weird group. Paranoia, isolation, and eccentricity define this wrestling stable.
cards.power: The Social Detachment.

cards.lore: Before age 15, called Conduct Disorder Charlie. Has no respect for the laws of the ring.
cards.power: The Rule Breaker. Strikes when the ref isn't looking. Feels no remorse and loves risk.

cards.lore: Massive fear of abandonment. Uses self-harm to dampen the inner pain.
cards.power: The Splitting Move. Today you are Bella's hero; tomorrow her worst enemy. Nothing in between.

cards.lore: Her feelings are like stage props: loud, colorful, but shallow. Needs validation like oxygen.
cards.power: The Spotlight Stealer. Cries, screams, or undresses — as long as all cameras are on her.

cards.lore: Under his giant ego hides a tiny self-esteem that breaks at the slightest criticism.
cards.power: The Mirror Worship. Convinced he is the only true champion. Everyone else is an extra.

cards.lore: Unlike Sid, Ava WANTS closeness, but her inferiority complexes keep her in the locker room.
cards.power: The Rejection Fear. Would love to join in, but convinced everyone will laugh at her.

cards.lore: Needs someone to take responsibility for her life. Alone, she feels completely helpless.
cards.power: The Decision Trap. Can't even choose which boots to wear without asking her coach.

cards.lore: Unlike OCD, Oliver LIKES his control obsession. He thinks everyone else is just sloppy.
cards.power: The Checklist Attack. Spends the whole match ironing the ropes and disinfecting the mat.

cards.lore: The worried group. Fear, uncertainty, and perfectionism prevent free combat.
cards.power: The Inhibition.

cards.lore: Alcohol withdrawal is the most dangerous. Without Garny (GABA), the brain goes haywire.
cards.power: The DT-Shake. When Al runs out of juice, the ring shakes. Confusion, fever, hallucinations.

cards.lore: Blocks pain signals in the spinal cord and dampens the respiratory center in the brainstem.
cards.power: The Slow Motion. Feels no more pain, but barely breathes. Drifts away.

cards.lore: Saves lives but triggers brutal, instant withdrawal. The wrestler wakes up screaming and vomiting.
cards.power: The Instant Wake-Up. Kicks the door down and throws Ollie off the receptors immediately.

cards.lore: Warning: Never give beta-blockers! Leads to an unopposed alpha strike — blood pressure shoots through the roof.
cards.power: The Heart Race. Infinite energy but makes the wrestler paranoid and aggressive.

cards.lore: A primitive defense to reduce the complexity of feelings.
cards.power: The Black & White Vision. Divides the world into heroes and traitors. No grey zone.

cards.lore: Protects his ego by searching for and fighting his own faults in others.
cards.power: The Mirror Toss. Throws his own unacceptable impulses onto his opponent.

cards.lore: Rage is shifted from the dangerous source to a safe target.
cards.power: The Angry Slide. Takes out his frustration on someone weaker or blameless.

cards.lore: The only healthy way. Dark energy is used for something good.
cards.power: The Rage Reform. Transforms her aggression into training and mastery.

cards.lore: Stimulants (methylphenidate) help switch his filter system back on.
cards.power: The Squirrel Chase. Cannot focus on his opponent because a butterfly is flying by.

cards.lore: Danger: refeeding syndrome! If she eats after a long time, phosphate drops and the heart fails.
cards.power: The Mirror Lie. Sees a giant in the mirror, though she's just skin and bones.

cards.lore: Violent reaction to D2 blockers (Hali). Therapy: stop med, cool down, give dantrolene.
cards.power: The Rigor Mortis Attack. Makes muscles as hard as iron bars. Life-threatening emergency!

cards.lore: Combo of SSRIs and MAOIs. Muscles over-cranked but not rigid like Mel's.
cards.power: The Shiver Shake. Too much Sally in the soup. Legs tremble uncontrollably (clonus).

cards.lore: If the Sentry says YES, the fight ends immediately — safety first!
cards.power: The Risk Check. Before the match begins, must check: Is the wrestler a danger to himself?

cards.lore: Without vitamin B1, the brain dies. Ken doesn't lie intentionally — he just fills the holes.
cards.power: The Memory Eraser. Walt is the emergency (give thiamine!); Ken is the lasting damage (invents stories).

cards.lore: Is it organic or psychiatric? Rule out the body before you blame the mind. Gestalt is dead. Stay fluffy!
cards.power: The Systemic Diagnosis.

cards.lore: MedKayfab Psychiatry Edition v1.0 complete. Mind the gap!
cards.power: Identify NMS-Mel (Lead-Pipe Fever), Diagnose Al-the-Alcoholic (48-Hour Shakes), Call Narcan-Nancy (Heroin Nod).

title: MedKayfab — Psychiatry Wrestling: The Mind-Bending Mat
